rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A moderate temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Change only gradient duration to identify which critical pairs respond to a shallower slope, particularly the near-coeluting late cluster. This diagnostic run will guide subsequent window and temperature optimization.

The shallower gradient improved some pairs but worsened another and incurred a time penalty. Test higher temperature at the original slope to shift selectivity in the critical clusters while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Raise the starting organic fraction to remove low-organic time while making the gradient shallower. This tests whether the late cluster can gain resolution without pushing the last peak beyond 10 minutes; the early peaks will reveal whether the higher start is tolerable.

Test the low-temperature endpoint at the original gradient to map selectivity changes across the full temperature range. Cooling may separate the early and late clusters in a different order while still keeping the last peak near 10 minutes.

Extend the promising high-temperature, higher-start approach with a shallower gradient while retaining a strong final solvent. This should improve the late critical pair and tests whether the early cluster remains sufficiently separated.

Test whether moving beyond the early-pair crossover restores its resolution while the shallower slope improves the late cluster. The preceding run leaves time headroom, but this injection will also check for excessive compression of the earliest peaks.

Compare directly with injection 4 to isolate temperature-dependent selectivity at the trimmed gradient. An intermediate temperature may improve the early three-peak cluster enough to offset any loss in the late cluster.

Lower the start slightly from injection 4 to improve early-peak retention and alter selectivity in the early cluster. This slope should retain much of the late-pair improvement while keeping the final peak close to, but below, 10 minutes.

Test a modest temperature reduction from the best method to move the early near-coeluting pair away from its apparent crossover. The existing time margin should accommodate cooling, allowing a direct assessment of the tradeoff against late-cluster resolution.
Refine injection 4 with a slightly shallower slope, using its remaining time margin to improve the late critical pair. Keeping the 0.15 start avoids the severe early-pair crossover seen at 0.20.

Explore the steeper-gradient side of the selectivity crossovers rather than only making the gradient shallower. Returning to the low start protects early retention, while this run tests whether the critical clusters separate better in a different elution order.

Use the best 0.20-start method's time margin for a shallower gradient by lowering the endpoint one step. This should improve the middle and late critical pairs while bringing the last peak close to the 10-minute scoring boundary.

Refine injection 11 by cooling one temperature step to improve the earliest pair and rebalance the early three-peak cluster. Its 0.26-minute time margin should largely accommodate this change while preserving the shallower-gradient gains.

Fine-tune the best method to a slightly shallower slope of 0.045 organic fraction per minute, targeting the remaining time margin below 10 minutes. The estimated last-peak elution fraction is about 0.62, so the 0.65 endpoint should still keep every peak within the gradient.

Revisit the low-start branch with a slope between injections 3 and 9, preserving the well-separated earliest pair while improving the early-cluster crossover and late pair. The last peak is expected just below 10 minutes, making this a promising alternative to the current best.

Test whether moderate cooling rescues the early separations at a 0.25 start, beyond the crossover limiting the current best method. The selected slope should keep the final peak near 10 minutes while assessing this alternative selectivity region.

Combine the shallower slope of injection 7 with moderate cooling to improve its early cluster and middle critical pair. This should use the available time margin while testing whether the 0.25-start branch can outperform the current best.

Explore one higher-start, cooler-temperature combination to move the early cluster farther beyond its crossover. The shallower slope may recover middle and late resolution, although this run explicitly tests the risk of compressing the earliest peaks.

Fine-tune the low-start branch to a slope of 0.065, slightly shallower than injection 16. This should improve all three remaining critical pairs while placing the last peak very close to the 10-minute boundary.

Refine the higher-start branch with an intermediate temperature and a shallower slope, targeting a final peak just below 10 minutes. This tests whether improved middle and late resolution can outweigh the temperature-dependent losses in the early cluster.

Test one slightly shallower slope than the best method to determine whether additional critical-pair resolution outweighs a small excursion beyond 10 minutes. This brackets the local resolution–time optimum at the most promising starting composition and temperature.

Test a shallower gradient on the 0.15-start branch to see whether its better-balanced early cluster can outperform the current best. A small time penalty is possible, but this brackets the remaining resolution–time tradeoff for that starting composition.

Fine-tune injection 17 with a slightly shallower slope, using its remaining time margin to improve the middle and late critical pairs. The predicted last peak is near 10 minutes, giving this cooler, higher-start branch a final competitive test.

Refine injection 18 with a slightly shallower slope, targeting its remaining time margin to improve the middle and late critical pairs. This is a final test of whether the higher-start branch can exceed the best CRF while keeping the last peak near 10 minutes.
